chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl ibn Bazīʿ, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from his father, who said:
Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: “A hadd carried out in the earth is purer for it than the rainfall of forty nights and their days.”

key_terms.الْأَرْضِ: the land or earth, meaning society and its domain
key_terms.قَطْرِ: falling drops, here referring to rainfall

ai.seo_question: Why is carrying out a hadd considered a purification for the land in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith states the great purifying effect of establishing a divinely prescribed legal punishment in the land. It emphasizes that the implementation of justice is a means of purification and public good greater than abundant rainfall.
